es.summary: Estado de falta o reducción significativa de movimiento que predispone a complicaciones sistémicas y locales.
key_points: Aumenta riesgo de úlceras por presión por presión prolongada sobre tejidos.
Favorece trombosis venosa profunda por estasis sanguínea.
Provoca atelectasias y disminución de la capacidad respiratoria.
Conduce a pérdida de masa muscular y disminución de la fuerza.
Compromete la nutrición, la eliminación y la integridad cutánea.

purpose: Prevenir complicaciones asociadas a la inmovilidad.
Mantener la integridad cutánea y la perfusión tisular.
Preservar la función respiratoria y cardiovascular.
Fomentar la independencia en actividades de la vida diaria.
procedure: Evaluar rango de movimiento activo y pasivo en todas las articulaciones.
Medir fuerza muscular con escala de Oxford (0‑5).
Determinar nivel de independencia usando la escala de Barthel.
Identificar factores de riesgo: edad, comorbilidades, incontinencia.
Planificar programa de movilización temprana y ejercicios de rango de movimiento.
safety: Verificar estabilidad del paciente antes de transferencias.
Utilizar dispositivos de ayuda (camas con barandillas, andadores).
Mantener el entorno libre de obstáculos y con buena iluminación.
Monitorear signos vitales durante actividades para detectar intolerancia.
nursing_care: Inspeccionar piel cada 2 h; registrar enrojecimiento, calor o edema.
Evaluar respiración: auscultar, observar expansión torácica y oxigenación.
Controlar ingesta y eliminación; registrar cambios en patrón intestinal.
Promover ejercicios de respiración profunda y tos asistida.
Reportar signos de trombosis (dolor, edema unilateral) o deterioro cutáneo.
documentation: Registrar hallazgos de la evaluación de movilidad y fuerza.
Anotar plan de turnos de reposicionamiento y ejercicios prescritos.
Documentar observaciones de piel, respiración y respuesta a intervenciones.
Incluir hora, responsable y cualquier evento adverso.

outcomes: Integridad cutánea: piel sin lesiones visibles en 48 h
Movilidad: aumento de actividad física mínima 30 min/día en 7 días

interventions.action: Reposicionar al paciente cada 2 h, alternando puntos de presión.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la presión prolongada y mejora la perfusión cutánea.

interventions.action: Inspeccionar la piel en áreas de riesgo (cóccix, talones, sacro) al menos cada 2 h.
interventions.rationale: Permite detección temprana de enrojecimiento o daño.
Distribuye la presión y disminuye la carga sobre tejidos vulnerables.

interventions.action: Realizar ejercicios de rango de movimiento activo‑pasivo de 5‑10 min, 3 veces al día.
interventions.rationale: Mantiene la circulación y la elasticidad muscular.

interventions.action: Asegurar ingesta adecuada de proteínas (1.2‑1.5 g/kg/día) y líquidos (≥30 mL/kg/día).
interventions.rationale: Favorece la integridad cutánea y la perfusión tisular.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente y familia sobre la importancia de la movilización y el autocuidado de la piel.
interventions.rationale: Promueve la adherencia al plan de prevención.

en.summary: State of lack or significant reduction of movement that predisposes to systemic and local complications.
key_points: Increases risk of pressure ulcers due to prolonged pressure on tissues.
Promotes deep venous thrombosis from blood stasis.
Causes atelectasis and decreased respiratory capacity.
Leads to loss of muscle mass and strength.
Compromises nutrition, elimination, and skin integrity.

purpose: Maintain skin integrity and tissue perfusion.
Promote independence in activities of daily living.
procedure: Assess active and passive range of motion in all joints.
Measure muscle strength with the Oxford scale (0‑5).
Determine level of independence using the Barthel Index.
Identify risk factors: age, comorbidities, incontinence.
Plan early mobilization program and range‑of‑motion exercises.
safety: Use assistive devices (beds with rails, walkers).
Keep environment free of obstacles and well lit.
Monitor vital signs during activities to detect intolerance.
nursing_care: Inspect skin every 2 h; record redness, warmth, or edema.
Assess breathing: auscultate, observe chest expansion, and oxygenation.
Monitor intake and elimination; record changes in bowel pattern.
Promote deep breathing exercises and assisted coughing.
Report signs of thrombosis (pain, unilateral edema) or skin deterioration.
documentation: Record findings from mobility and strength assessment.
Note repositioning schedule and prescribed exercises.
Document skin, respiratory, and response observations.
Include time, responsible staff, and any adverse events.

outcomes: Skin integrity: no visible lesions within 48 h
Mobility: increase in minimal physical activity to 30 min/day within 7 days

interventions.action: Reposition the patient every 2 h, alternating pressure points.
interventions.rationale: Reduces prolonged pressure and improves skin perfusion.

interventions.action: Inspect skin in risk areas (coccyx, heels, sacrum) at least every 2 h.
interventions.rationale: Allows early detection of redness or damage.
Distributes pressure and decreases load on vulnerable tissues.

interventions.action: Perform active‑passive range‑of‑motion exercises for 5‑10 min, three times daily.
Ensure adequate protein intake (1.2‑1.5 g/kg/day) and fluids (≥30 mL/kg/day).
interventions.rationale: Supports skin integrity and tissue perfusion.

interventions.action: Educate patient and family on importance of mobilization and skin self‑care.

sources.name: Fundamentals of Nursing: Considerations for Care of Neuromuscular Impairment

key_points.0.quote: A pressure injury is defined as breakdown of skin integrity caused by prolonged internal pressure against a bony prominence or persistent contact with an external surface (e.g., furniture, medical or other devices) often in combination with shear.

key_points.1.quote: The pooling blood in the legs also increases a patient’s risk for venous thrombus formation and orthostatic hypotension.

key_points.2.quote: Lack of deep breathing deconditions the respiratory muscles and diminishes lung expansion.

sections.purpose.0.quote: Promoting mobility can prevent these complications from occurring.

sections.purpose.3.quote: Occupational therapists can provide training and adaptive equipment to promote independence and maximize functional abilities in daily activities.

sections.procedure.1.quote: A common method of evaluating muscle strength is the Medical Research Council Manual Muscle Testing scale ( Table 9.4 ).

sections.safety.1.quote: Additionally, the use of adaptive equipment and assistive devices (e.g., wheelchairs, walkers, canes) can restore some mobility, allowing for increased independence and participation in self-care activities.

sections.documentation.0.quote: Assessment of strength is important to establish a baseline for intervention evaluations.

sections.documentation.1.quote: For instance, the nurse should encourage the patient to perform active or passive range of motion exercises as prescribed by the physical therapist or if necessary perform these ADLs for the patient.
